requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1, storing dated archives under /var/backups/inventory.
requirements.summary: Node1 has a permanent 02:17 daily cron entry. Automatic cron invocation was demonstrated with a temporary accelerated schedule, an archive named inventory-2026-10-04.tar.gz was created in the required directory, and a 4 KiB source test file had the same SHA-256 hash inside the archive. A cross-node backup also succeeded after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain backups for the last seven days.
requirements.summary: The actual backup workflow deleted a fixture aged eight days while retaining one aged six days, directly demonstrating the configured retention behavior.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The solution uses the existing OpenSSH, tar, gzip, cron, and shell stack; selected package versions remained present, rsync remained uninstalled, package-health checks passed, and SELinux remained enforcing.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: nightly scheduling and accurate cross-node archive creation, seven-day retention, and preservation of the legacy RHEL release and kernel. Restart evidence is strong and independently corroborated. Hygiene is high, with only two small restart-log files left in /tmp.
limitations: The permanent 02:17 schedule was not observed at its natural execution time; cron-driven execution was demonstrated using a temporary every-minute entry that invoked the same script and was subsequently removed.

After functional-test cleanup, the source directory was empty, so the final post-restart archive contained no regular files. Accurate non-empty transfer was demonstrated earlier with a temporary 4 KiB file and matching source/archive SHA-256 hashes.

Lifecycle package-health snapshots are bounded and do not provide a complete before/after RPM inventory, though platform snapshots and direct final package checks support preservation of the required release, kernel, and software stack.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation and bounded validation mutations were causally related to the task; temporary source data, retention fixtures, and the accelerated cron proof were removed. The only identified unnecessary retained mutations are /tmp/inventory-restart.log on node1 and node2, created by the restart commands and left behind after verification. These are small, low-risk abandoned files. No failed services, damaged package state, or new network exposure was observed. The provider-wide restart protocol was otherwise complete on both nodes: healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement and observed interruption, different post-restart boot IDs, recovered services/configuration/data, and a successful post-restart cross-node backup; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
